themes.label: ARCH-to-GARCH motivation and paper roadmap
themes.need: Someone surveying whether a longer-memory GARCH specification is warranted for their own volatility model needs the motivation for generalizing ARCH's fixed-lag structure and its relation to the AR-to-ARMA generalization.
themes.distributed_justification: b001-b003 form one continuous background-and-contribution narrative; the gap at lines 18-19 is Pass-A trash (author acknowledgment footnote), not a thematic break.

themes.label: GARCH(p,q) definition and stationarity condition
themes.need: Someone specifying a GARCH(p,q) conditional-variance model needs the equation form and parameter constraints, its ARCH(infinity)/regression formulations, and the wide-sense stationarity condition (Theorem 1) together with its proof to confirm the process is well-defined and stationary.
themes.distributed_justification: The GARCH(p,q) definition/stationarity claim (b005-b011, lines 26-99) and its formal proof (appendix A.1, b042-b044) are two parts of one need - stating a stationarity condition and verifying it; trash conversion-residue lines (402-403, 454-455) split the proof into three sub-spans without breaking the argument.

themes.label: GARCH(1,1) moment-existence condition (Theorem 2)
themes.need: Someone fitting a GARCH(1,1) model needs the necessary-and-sufficient condition for existence of the 2m-th moment (Theorem 2), its recursive formula, and the underlying proof to check whether their estimated parameters admit finite higher moments.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2's moment-existence condition (b012-b014) and its formal proof (appendix A.2, b045) are two parts of one need - stating a moment condition and its derivation.

themes.label: GARCH(1,1) lag and kurtosis diagnostics
themes.need: Someone interpreting a fitted GARCH(1,1) model's persistence and tail behavior needs the mean-lag and median-lag formulas and the fourth-moment/kurtosis expressions to characterize how quickly shocks decay and how fat-tailed the process is.
themes.distributed_justification: The mean-lag formula (b015) and the median-lag/fourth-moment/kurtosis formulas (b016-b018) are both diagnostics computed from the same GARCH(1,1) framework; a Fig.1 caption (trash, lines 142-144) separates them in the raw text.

themes.label: Squared-process ACF/PACF for model identification
themes.need: Someone trying to identify or diagnose the order of a GARCH model from data needs the theoretical autocorrelation and partial-autocorrelation behavior of the squared process (its ARMA-type recursion, Yule-Walker analogue, and PACF cutoff) to match observed sample ACF/PACF patterns to a candidate specification.

themes.label: Maximum likelihood estimation of GARCH regression
themes.need: Someone implementing maximum-likelihood estimation for a GARCH regression model needs the log-likelihood function, the score and information-matrix expressions for mean and variance parameters, and the BHHH iterative algorithm with its asymptotic properties.

themes.label: Lagrange multiplier test for GARCH presence
themes.need: Someone wanting to test statistically whether GARCH effects are present in their data needs the Lagrange multiplier test statistic, its T*R^2 computational form, and the caveat that a general test is infeasible when both AR and MA orders are positive.

themes.label: Empirical inflation-rate GARCH application
themes.need: Someone validating a GARCH(1,1) specification against a real case needs to see how it is set up, estimated, and diagnostically compared against OLS and a fixed-lag ARCH(8) model on actual inflation-rate data, including fit statistics, kurtosis/skewness, lag comparisons, and forecast-interval behavior.
themes.distributed_justification: The inflation-rate empirical case (setup, model comparisons, diagnostics, and forecast-interval interpretation) is one continuous application; figure captions for Figs. 2-4 (trash, lines 361-363/374-376/381-383) interrupt the prose without breaking the underlying case-study narrative.

unassigned.reason: Purely navigational meta-text (section-by-section roadmap of the paper's own structure) - answers no practitioner information need, so including it in t01 would violate R5's 'only' (precision) half.
